subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: On normal gateway SIGTERM/SIGINT, should OpenClaw cancel managed active/background exec child processes before the shutdown watchdog, preserve yielded/background work, or defer child-process control to a separate session/process operator surface?
rationale: Current tests deliberately preserve active/background work on normal shutdown, while fixing this report likely changes that lifecycle contract or adds a bounded exception for managed child processes.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: Normal stop would reject new work, drain briefly, then cancel managed exec/process scopes before the watchdog while documenting explicit preservation exceptions.

options.title: Preserve background work and improve diagnostics
options.body: OpenClaw would keep the current normal-stop contract and add diagnostics that identify the child process responsible for shutdown timeout.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: This issue would wait for the broader session-scoped process list/kill surface tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: Normal stop would reject new work, drain briefly, then cancel managed exec/process scopes before the watchdog while documenting explicit preservation exceptions.
